question: Can the apparent reparametrization dependence of neural-network optimization, Hessian flatness, and parameter-density modes be removed by treating parameter space as a Riemannian manifold and explicitly transforming its metric together with every geometric object?

key_findings.claim: The paper's central guardrail is mathematically sound but narrower than its rhetoric: coordinate representations of a fixed geometric construction agree when a diffeomorphic coordinate change and every tensor transformation rule, including the metric, are applied consistently.
key_findings.evidence: The paper distinguishes a change of coordinates between two parameter-space representations from a weight-space symmetry within one representation. It gives the standard rules: vectors transform by J, covectors by J^-T, and a metric by J^-T G J^-1. Inner products and other properly contracted quantities are then coordinate invariant by construction. This is a useful correction to analyses that silently reset the metric to identity after changing coordinates, but it does not make different metrics, models, priors, or optimization algorithms equivalent.

key_findings.claim: The intended Hessian result is correct after repair, but the paper's principal derivation repeatedly drops the inverse on the metric and therefore does not prove what it claims.
key_findings.evidence: The invariant endomorphism should be E=G^-1 H. From G-hat=J^-T G J^-1 and H-hat=J^-T H J^-1, direct algebra gives E-hat=J G^-1 H J^-1=J E J^-1, which preserves determinant, trace, and eigenvalues. Equation 2 instead prints J G H J^-1, then equates det(GH) with det(E). Appendices B.2-B.3 reuse the same G H expression in Equations 10-11. An independent diagonal check with G=diag(2,3), H=diag(5,7), and J=diag(4,6) gives the correct eigenvalues 2.5 and 7/3 before and after transformation, while the printed right-hand side has eigenvalues 10 and 21. Appendix A happens to work because it directly retains the inverse of the transformed identity metric.

key_findings.claim: Metric-conditioned Hessian spectra are coordinate invariant but remain metric dependent, so reparametrization consistency alone cannot make flatness an intrinsic predictor of generalization or support the paper's 'definitive' cross-optimizer comparison.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing coordinates while carrying one fixed metric leaves the generalized spectrum invariant, but replacing G by cG rescales every eigenvalue of G^-1 H by 1/c without changing the network or its generalization. The paper explicitly permits any positive-definite metric, yet Figure 5 compares SGD under the Euclidean metric with ADAM under an undefined gradient-second-moment metric and concludes that ADAM is definitively sharper. ADAM also has first-moment and time-dependent optimizer state, so no position-only G(theta), state selection, damping, or cross-metric normalization is specified. Coordinate invariance within each geometry does not make numerical sharpness values across different geometries commensurate.

key_findings.claim: The optimization section establishes covariance of a continuous-time Riemannian gradient flow, not invariance of the ordinary discrete gradient-descent algorithm used in practice.
key_findings.evidence: Starting from theta-dot=-G^-1 grad L and transforming G produces the same geometric trajectory in new coordinates; this is a standard coordinate-covariance statement. In the new coordinates, Euclidean GD from theta becomes a Jacobian-preconditioned flow, not ordinary identity-metric GD in psi. The authors acknowledge that discrete updates are only approximately invariant and worsen with step size, but provide no geometric integrator or implementation. The practical distinction of natural gradient is therefore not that other flows lack a coordinate representation, but that the Fisher and related pullback matrices can sometimes be recomputed with the correct transformation automatically, subject to approximation, damping, and singularity.

key_findings.claim: The density-mode construction is coordinate consistent only after choosing and preserving a particular base geometry; modes are not an inherent property of a probability measure independent of that choice.
key_findings.evidence: The paper correctly rewrites a Lebesgue density q as q^G=q/sqrt(det G), the Radon-Nikodym density with respect to the Riemannian volume dV_G, and shows that q^G transforms as a scalar when G is transformed. However, choosing another metric changes both dV_G and generally the maximizer of q^G. Thus the construction resolves coordinate dependence conditional on a chosen metric but does not select a unique MAP notion. The Fisher example is also unavailable as a Riemannian volume on the overparameterized neural networks that the paper itself notes have singular Fisher matrices.

key_findings.claim: The Laplace marginal-likelihood application is mathematically invalid as printed in several independent ways.
key_findings.evidence: For negative log posterior L_MAP with Hessian H, the Gaussian integral is exp(-L_MAP)(2pi)^(d/2)det(H)^(-1/2), so its log is -L_MAP+d/2 log(2pi)-1/2 log det H. Main Equation 5 prints the opposite signs for both normalization terms; Appendix E.3 additionally drops the one-half on log det and calls N(theta_MAP,H) the Gaussian although H is the precision and the covariance is H^-1. The appendix proves only that a quadratic scalar integrand is preserved, then declares its integral preserved while ignoring the transformed integration measure and its Jacobian. It also treats theta-theta_MAP as an exactly transforming tangent vector, which fails for a nonlinear coordinate map away from the expansion point. A one-dimensional H=9 check gives the correct normalization log -0.17967, the main formula +0.17967, and the appendix formula +1.27829.

anchors.section: Appendix E.3, Gaussian normalization and invariance argument

key_findings.claim: The WeightNorm demonstration falls outside the paper's own reparametrization framework and does not empirically validate a corrected Laplace evidence.
key_findings.evidence: The framework assumes a bijective smooth map with smooth inverse between equal-dimensional coordinate spaces. The paper states that WeightNorm introduces more parameters than the Cartesian network even though degrees of freedom are intended to match; the standard unconstrained WeightNorm map has a scale redundancy and is not such a diffeomorphism. Table 1 reports only two different naive values, -212.7 versus -227.1, and no corrected invariant value. The accompanying text calls the transformed value 'trivially invariant' without supplying a computation, while the formulas used to justify it are wrong.

key_findings.claim: The framework deliberately excludes the non-identifiability and symmetry structure that dominates actual overparameterized neural-network weight spaces.
key_findings.evidence: The main analysis is restricted to coordinate charts connected by diffeomorphisms and explicitly leaves group-action symmetries for future work. It also detaches parameter space from the model-distribution manifold because the latter is not bijective and its pullback Fisher is singular. This produces clean positive-definite geometry, but it means permutations, ReLU rescalings, redundant WeightNorm coordinates, rank-deficient Fisher/GGN matrices, and many-to-one parameter-to-function maps are not solved by the paper's theory. The 2024 successor by Roy et al. instead formulates effective-parameter equivalence classes and a quotient/pseudo-metric view precisely for this missing setting.

key_findings.claim: The infinite-width discussion is a conceptual relabeling of conventions that change function scaling, priors, and hyperparameters, not a new invariant limit theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The paper argues that standard and NTK 'parametrizations' are not mere coordinate representations because the commonly compared conventions define different forward functions and priors; if every object were pushed through a true coordinate map, the finite-width function and metric-aware tangent kernel would agree. That bookkeeping point is useful. But the appendix then recapitulates standard NNGP/NTK calculations, changes both architecture scaling and prior, offers no new convergence result or experiment, and describes different limiting behavior that follows precisely because it chose different models rather than re-expressions of one model.

anchors.section: Appendix E.1, invariant NTK and prior comparison

key_findings.claim: The release is a paper-source bundle rather than a reproducible research artifact.
key_findings.evidence: The exact arXiv v3 archive contains 58 files: TeX, bibliography/style/build metadata, TikZ sources, rendered figures, and several unused draft assets. The official NeurIPS supplement is only Appendices A-E. There is no experiment code, environment, dependency lock, raw data, checkpoints, commands, seed list, hardware record, or output logs. Raw Figure 5 bar heights and Tables 1-3 are embedded in TeX/TikZ, and Table 2 alone says accuracies average five seeds. The toy Laplace setup gives 150 samples, a one-hidden-layer tanh network, and 1,000 epochs but omits width, optimizer, prior, likelihood, WeightNorm details, and seeds; the optimizer experiment is similarly insufficient to replay.

method.core_idea: Treat a neural network's parameter space as a Riemannian manifold, keep the metric explicit, and push functions, vectors, covectors, Hessians, metrics, flows, and base measures through a diffeomorphic coordinate change according to their tensor types so that downstream quantities represent the same abstract objects.
method.mechanism: A reparametrization psi=phi(theta) induces Jacobian J. Tangent vectors use J, covectors use J^-T, and the metric uses J^-T G J^-1. The Riemannian gradient is G^-1 times the differential; the Hessian bilinear form is raised to an endomorphism E=G^-1 H; and Lebesgue density q is converted to q/sqrt(det G) relative to Riemannian volume. The paper then applies this bookkeeping to continuous gradient flows, Hessian spectra, density modes, standard-versus-NTK scaling conventions, Laplace evidence, and optimizer-associated sharpness.
assumptions: The compared parameterizations are coordinate charts on the same smooth manifold and are connected by a bijective differentiable map with differentiable inverse.
The parameter-space metric is smooth and positive definite, so it has an inverse and defines a Riemannian volume form.
One fixed metric and every relevant geometric object are transformed consistently rather than silently redefined in new coordinates.
Hessian invariants are evaluated with the full Riemannian Hessian, or at a critical point where the connection term vanishes.
Optimization trajectories are continuous-time flows; ordinary finite-step updates only approximate the claimed invariance.
The chosen metric is scientifically meaningful in addition to being coordinate consistent.
Probability-density modes are defined relative to the chosen Riemannian base measure rather than treated as properties of a measure without a reference volume.
The optimizer preconditioner can be represented as a position-dependent positive-definite metric despite momentum, damping, and time-dependent state.
The Fisher or GGN is nonsingular when it is used as a Riemannian metric, contrary to the common overparameterized case.
Laplace calculations correctly transform the measure, local displacement, mode, metric, and Hessian; the printed application violates several of these requirements.

techniques.role: Represent one abstract parameter manifold in alternative coordinates.
Carry the parameter-space geometry through the Jacobian transformation.
Distinguish vector and covector transformation rules and raise differentials with the metric.
Include connection coefficients away from critical points.
Raise one Hessian index to form G^-1 H and generalized spectral invariants.
Express preconditioned optimization as a continuous Riemannian flow.
Define coordinate-scalar densities relative to sqrt(det G) dtheta.
Identify Fisher, GGN, and empirical-Fisher matrices as automatically covariant pullback families under restricted conditions.
Distinguish a true coordinate change from simultaneous changes to architecture and prior in width limits.
Inspect all pages, equations, figures, tables, appendices, TeX, TikZ, and official supplement.
Re-derive Hessian similarity transforms and Gaussian normalization independently.
Use diagonal metrics and a one-dimensional Gaussian integral to expose printed algebra errors.
Assess source contents and the absence of executable experimental materials.

evaluations.setting: Analytic scaling phi(theta)=3 theta for L(theta)=sum_i theta_i^2.
evaluations.metric: Determinant of the raw Hessian versus the metric-conditioned Hessian operator.
evaluations.result: The raw determinant changes from 2^d to (2/9)^d, while explicitly transforming the Euclidean metric makes det(G^-1 H)=2^d in both coordinates.
evaluations.baseline: Autodiff Hessian with the metric silently reset to identity after reparametrization.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 SGD minima rescaled by one-half and two, averaged over five stated seeds.
evaluations.metric: Generalization gap and raw Hessian trace.
evaluations.result: The generalization gap stays 5.2 plus or minus 0.2 points while raw trace changes from 1531.8 to 6143.7 or 383.6, correctly illustrating non-invariance of unconditioned sharpness.
evaluations.baseline: ADAM without reparametrization, with 7.2 plus or minus 0.2 generalization gap and trace 1929.8 plus or minus 61.2.

evaluations.setting: LeNet on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST and WideResNet-16-4 on CIFAR-10/100, trained for 100 epochs with SGD or default ADAM.
evaluations.metric: Log Hessian trace with Euclidean H for SGD, raw H for ADAM, and an optimizer-metric E for ADAM; plus test accuracy.
evaluations.result: Embedded plot values put SGD and raw-ADAM log traces around 7.4-8.4 and metric-conditioned ADAM around 24.8-25.8; Table 2 gives SGD higher test accuracy on all four tasks. The ADAM metric/state is undefined and no uncertainty is shown for Figure 5, so cross-geometry sharpness is not reproducible or definitive.
evaluations.baseline: Raw Euclidean Hessian trace and SGD's identity-metric operator.

evaluations.setting: Toy 150-point sine regression with a one-hidden-layer tanh network, comparing Cartesian and WeightNorm parameterizations.
evaluations.metric: The paper's stated Laplace log marginal likelihood and its loss/rest decomposition.
evaluations.result: Naive values differ, -212.7 plus or minus 3.4 versus -227.1 plus or minus 3.6. No corrected value is reported, WeightNorm is not a diffeomorphic equal-dimensional chart, and the defining Laplace formulas are wrong.
evaluations.baseline: Cartesian parameterization versus a redundantly parameterized WeightNorm implementation.

evaluations.setting: Independent symbolic/numeric audit of the general Hessian-operator transform.
evaluations.metric: Agreement of E and transformed E spectra under a nonidentity diagonal metric and coordinate scaling.
evaluations.result: Direct computation preserves eigenvalues 2.5 and 7/3 under J E J^-1; the paper's printed J G H J^-1 yields 10 and 21, confirming the missing inverse is substantive.

evaluations.setting: Independent one-dimensional Gaussian-integral audit with curvature H=9 and zero mode loss.
evaluations.result: The correct value is one-half log(2pi) minus one-half log 9, or -0.17967. Main Equation 5 gives +0.17967 and Appendix E.3 gives +1.27829, while its invariance proof additionally omits the integration-measure Jacobian.

evaluations.setting: Reproducibility audit of arXiv v3 source and the official NeurIPS supplement.
evaluations.metric: Availability of code, environment, data, commands, raw results, seeds, and sufficient experiment specification.
evaluations.result: TeX/TikZ and embedded result values are available, but there is no executable artifact and none of the empirical claims can be independently replayed from the release.
evaluations.baseline: A versioned end-to-end research artifact with one command per table and figure.

limitations: Author-stated: the work is a consistency guardrail, not a better optimizer, preconditioner, or generalization measure.
Author-stated: it studies reparametrization but leaves neural-network group symmetries to future work.
Author-stated: discrete optimization is only approximately invariant, with error increasing with step size.
Author-stated: structured metric approximations, damping, and momentum restrict or break automatic transformation behavior.
Reviewer audit: the main and appendix Hessian proofs systematically omit G^-1 even though the intended similarity-transform result is repairable.
Reviewer audit: coordinate invariance does not choose a metric or make sharpness values under different metrics comparable.
Reviewer audit: the density mode depends on the selected base metric, and common Fisher/GGN choices are singular in overparameterized networks.
Reviewer audit: the Laplace formula, Gaussian covariance, measure transformation, and WeightNorm demonstration are invalid as printed.
Reviewer audit: the theory assumes diffeomorphic equal-dimensional charts and excludes the redundant/non-identifiable structure of practical neural networks.
Reviewer audit: ADAM is reduced to an undefined gradient-second-moment metric despite momentum and time-dependent state.
Reviewer audit: the experiments are small illustrations with no released code, raw runs, hardware, seed list, or adequate hyperparameter record.
Reviewer audit: the infinite-width section supplies a conceptual convention distinction rather than a new theorem or empirical result.
failure_modes: Resetting a transformed metric to identity changes the geometry rather than merely changing coordinates.
Using the printed J G H J^-1 formula instead of J G^-1 H J^-1 destroys the claimed generalized eigenvalues, trace, and determinant.
Applying an ordinary Euclidean discrete update in both coordinate systems produces different algorithms and trajectories.
Finite step size, approximate linear solves, damping, momentum, or factorized curvature can break exact flow covariance.
A singular Fisher or GGN cannot be inverted or define the positive Riemannian volume assumed by the paper.
Changing the base metric can move a density mode even though each chosen metric yields coordinate-consistent modes.
Comparing curvature values computed under different arbitrary metric scales can reverse any flat-versus-sharp conclusion.
The printed Laplace normalizer returns the reciprocal curvature dependence and can reverse model-evidence rankings.
Ignoring the Jacobian of the integration measure makes equal scalar integrands appear to have equal integrals when their coordinate volumes differ.
Treating a finite coordinate difference as an exactly transforming tangent vector fails under nonlinear reparametrization.
A redundant WeightNorm map, permutation, or ReLU scaling orbit is not a bijective chart transition and lies outside the analysis.
Without code and raw results, embedded plot values cannot reveal implementation, stochastic, or transcription errors.
reusable_insights: Always state whether a neural-network transformation is a coordinate change, a symmetry, or a change of model, prior, or algorithm.
Gradients are metric-raised differentials; confusing vector and covector representations is a common source of false invariance claims.
At a critical point, coordinate-invariant Hessian spectra are generalized eigenvalues of H v=lambda G v, equivalently the spectrum of G^-1 H.
The correct transformed Hessian operator is a similarity transform J E J^-1, providing a compact algebraic test for derivations and implementations.
Coordinate invariance and metric independence are different requirements; the former is automatic once a metric is fixed, while the latter generally fails.
A density mode is defined relative to a base measure; choosing Riemannian volume makes it coordinate consistent but exposes the scientific choice of metric.
Continuous vector-field covariance should not be advertised as invariance of an off-the-shelf finite-step optimizer without a geometric integrator and error analysis.
Gaussian-integral formulas should be unit-tested in one dimension before being used for marginal-likelihood invariance arguments.
Laplace evidence on a manifold must transform the local quadratic, volume form, mode definition, and determinant together.
Quotient or stratified geometry is needed for neural parameter symmetries and rank-deficient pullback metrics; a chart-only treatment is insufficient.
Optimizer-state geometry should live on an augmented state space if momentum or adaptive moments affect the dynamics.
Embedding raw plot arrays in TeX is useful for audit, but not a substitute for executable code and run-level records.
open_questions: Can the Hessian sections be corrected throughout by restoring G^-1 and adding regression tests for nonidentity metrics?
What metric-selection principle makes invariant sharpness scientifically predictive rather than merely coordinate consistent?
How should curvature values be normalized before comparing optimizers that induce different or time-varying geometries?
Can ADAM's full momentum and second-moment dynamics be represented invariantly on an augmented manifold and discretized equivariantly?
Which geometric integrators provide useful finite-step reparametrization accuracy at neural-network scale?
How should density modes and priors be defined when Fisher/GGN pullbacks are singular and the parameter-to-function map has strata?
Can the Laplace section be replaced by a correct Riemannian-volume derivation with the proper determinant, metric factor, and nonlinear local coordinates?
What does a valid WeightNorm experiment look like on a quotient chart with redundancy removed?
Do corrected invariant evidence rankings improve actual model selection compared with standard and linearized Laplace methods?
Which symmetry classes beyond diffeomorphic reparametrizations can be handled computationally through quotient or path geometry?
Can the Figure 5 and Table 1-3 experiments be recovered with exact code, data splits, seeds, optimizer state, and raw results?
Which claims about standard, NTK, and feature-learning limits survive when architecture, prior, learning rate, and coordinate map are varied one at a time?

competitive_landscape.title: A Reparametrization-Invariant Sharpness Measure Based on Information Geometry
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct prior work on the paper's Hessian-flatness motivation, explicitly cited by the reviewed paper.
competitive_landscape.difference: Jang et al. choose information geometry to define a concrete invariant sharpness measure, connect it theoretically to generalization, and use it as a training regularizer. The reviewed paper instead argues that any consistently transformed metric gives coordinate invariance, which is more general as bookkeeping but does not resolve metric selection or deliver a validated generalization method.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2022, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35

competitive_landscape.title: FAM: Relative Flatness Aware Minimization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous practical alternative for reparametrization-aware flatness and generalization.
competitive_landscape.difference: FAM derives an efficient single-layer relative-flatness regularizer and evaluates it across training and fine-tuning tasks with released code. It covers a narrower invariance family than arbitrary diffeomorphic chart changes but addresses the operational question the reviewed paper explicitly declines: using invariant flatness to improve generalization.

competitive_landscape.title: Riemannian Laplace Approximation with the Fisher Metric
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct metric-aware Laplace competitor that tests how geometric choice changes approximation quality.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu et al. show that Riemannian Laplace behavior depends heavily on the metric, identify asymptotic bias and overconcentration in a prior construction, derive Fisher-based variants, and evaluate them with released software. That evidence reinforces the missing distinction in the reviewed paper between coordinate invariance for a fixed metric and correctness or usefulness across metric choices.

competitive_landscape.title: Reparameterization Invariance in Approximate Bayesian Inference
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strongest direct post-publication successor, with overlapping authorship, for the density and Laplace claims.
competitive_landscape.difference: Roy et al. work in effective-parameter equivalence classes, relate quotient topology to a rank-deficient pullback pseudo-metric, analyze linearized Laplace invariance, and give a Riemannian-diffusion sampling algorithm with empirical posterior-fit results. It confronts neural non-identifiability and singular geometry that the reviewed paper removes by assumption, and supplies an executable inference method rather than a base-measure argument.

competitive_landscape.title: A Rescaling-Invariant Lipschitz Bound Based on Path-Metrics for Modern ReLU Network Parameterizations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current symmetry-aware alternative for parameter-space robustness, the main class the reviewed paper leaves untreated.
competitive_landscape.difference: Gonon et al. build an explicitly neuron-rescaling-invariant path metric for modern ReLU DAGs, prove a sharper Lipschitz bound computable in two forward passes, and demonstrate a rescaling-immune pruning criterion on ImageNet. It is limited to a structured symmetry rather than arbitrary coordinate charts, but delivers computable guarantees on realistic architectures and directly handles function-preserving rescalings.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A unifying Riemannian-geometric guardrail showing that Hessian flatness, gradient-descent trajectories, and density modes are inherently invariant under neural-network reparametrization when the implicit metric and its associated transformation rules are made explicit, with applications to infinite-width networks, Laplace model evidence, and optimizer bias.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper clearly packages coordinate geometry for an ML audience, distinguishes symmetries from chart changes, emphasizes vector/covector/metric bookkeeping, and connects Hessian, optimization, and density examples in one presentation. It was accepted at NeurIPS 2023. However, invariant information-geometric sharpness, natural-gradient covariance, invariant MAP constructions, and tensor transformation rules predate it, and the paper explicitly does not propose a new optimizer or metric.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The durable novelty is pedagogical synthesis and a useful diagnostic vocabulary, not the underlying differential geometry or a new practical method. The repaired statement that G^-1 H transforms by similarity is valuable, but its published proof is algebraically wrong. The probability result is conditional on an arbitrary base metric, continuous-flow covariance does not confer discrete-algorithm invariance, and the Laplace application is invalid. The strongest later successor, Roy et al. 2024, tackles quotient/pseudo-metric geometry and supplies an algorithm, while Jang, FAM, Yu, and Gonon give more operational approaches to invariant sharpness, metric-aware inference, or symmetries. The paper remains a useful warning against silently changing geometry, but its claimed applications require substantial correction and validation.

reviewer_notes: Audit covered all 20 pages of the exact arXiv v3 PDF, every equation and cancellation mark, six rendered figures, Tables 1-3, all 78 references, and Appendices A-E. All pages had usable extracted text. The exact PDF hash matched the pinned index. The arXiv source archive had SHA-256 eea8e2c70e82c2a2a93e7fa68b0dac9b3c1319b982fd6ad2fa12ecc208bc3a4d and contained 58 files; all used TeX/TikZ content and figures, build metadata, unused draft sections, and unused visual assets were inspected. The official NeurIPS supplemental PDF is only the seven appendix pages already present on pages 14-20. No associated experimental code or result archive was found in the paper, source, official proceedings record, or targeted title/author repository search. The Hessian and Gaussian counterchecks were derived independently and evaluated numerically without relying on the authors' formulas. No empirical rerun was possible because the artifact contains no executable experiment. Current primary competitors were checked from NeurIPS, PMLR, OpenReview, and arXiv records through 2026-08-24.
